\caption{Welfare comparison across the closure matrix. The layout mirrors
Table~\ref{tab:results-matrix} exactly --- the same three financing closures
(rows) crossed with the same five labour-market closures (columns), with the
elastic-supply column bracketed the same way --- but the variables reported in
each cell are welfare reads of the identical allocation rather than macro
outcomes, all in percent against the reference continuation. $W_C$ is the
household-consumption index of Table~\ref{tab:results-matrix}; $W_D$ the
quantity index of demand, i.e.\ the own-weights aggregate over $c+g$;
$W_{CES}$ the CES evaluation of that bundle at the \emph{baseline}
preference weights, which is what prices the composition shift the programme
imposes; $W_{CES^*}$ the same bundle evaluated at the \emph{adopted} weights,
read off the counterfactual bundle itself with $g$ subsumed into the private
part; and $W^{L}$ the first-order leisure-augmented form, which also
charges the household for the additional work a programme requires.
It is expressed on the household's resources rather than on a consumption basket,
so the treatment of saving has to be stated; the conservative reading, in which
saving is a leak that never returns, is the one tabulated here, and the deferred
alternative is discussed in the text.
$\eta_{s,i}\in\{0.5,1,2\}$, as in
Table~\ref{tab:results-matrix}.
}
\label{tab:welfare-comparison}
